chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Abu Maryam al-Ansari said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the boy who has not reached puberty; if a man accuses him (of zina), is he flogged? He said: No. And that is because if a man accuses the boy, he is not flogged.
ai.seo_question: Is a man flogged for accusing a pre-pubescent boy of zina?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) derives the ruling from the principle of *qiyas* (analogical reasoning), noting that since a pre-pubescent boy is not liable for *hadd* punishment due to his lack of full legal responsibility (*taklif*), an accuser targeting him is similarly exempt from flogging. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the correlation between the accused's status and the severity of the penalty in *qadhf* cases. The ruling underscores the mercy and precision in applying corporal punishments within the framework of *fiqh al-jafari*.
